summary: The recorded base reproduced loss of complete second and third GLM-4.7 tool calls in a final streaming increment. At the exact candidate commit, the checked-out source drained all complete calls with sequential indices, preserved a partial suffix for later completion, and passed focused and related parser tests.

tests.what_was_measured: On the actual recorded base, a final increment with two no-argument calls emitted only index 0 and retained the complete second call. Independent argument-bearing and three-call inputs showed the same one-call-only behavior.

At the exact candidate, two no-argument calls, two typed-argument calls, and three complete calls were all emitted in one invocation with sequential indices; a partial second call remained resumable and completed on the next increment.
The candidate's focused GLM-4.7 regression suite passed: 15 tests.
The related GLM-4 and GLM-4.7 parser suites passed: 29 tests.

gpu_execution_evidence: The reviewed defect and candidate change are CPU-only incremental text parsing. One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-) was visible through Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2/HIP 7.2.26015, but no GPU execution is relevant or claimed.
remaining_limitations: No GLM-4.7 model weights or full HTTP serving reproduction was used; validation covers the actual streaming detector implementation and its integration-level unit suite, not model semantic accuracy.
No distributed or multi-node workload was run.
No native rebuild was performed because the candidate changes only Python parser source, tests, and reports; no C++, FlyDSL, compiler, or native library path changed.
Ordinary text after the last tool call remains buffered pending another increment, a pre-existing single-call behavior outside the original multiple-complete-call contract.
